sentences.text:
Criminal Petition No.7986 Of 2019
Order:
1. Heard Sri Raja Reddy Koneti, learned counsel for the petitioners, and learned Public Prosecutor.
2. The petitioners have invoked the inherent jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 of the Cod

e of Criminal Procedure, 1973 with a prayer to quash the proceedings in C.C. No.659 of 2018, on the file of Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Addanki, Prakasam district, registered for the offences under Sections 273 and 188 R/w.34 of IPC and Sections 58, 59 and 63 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short, 'the FSS Act'), primarily on the ground that in similar circumstances this Court has interfered and quashed the proceedings in Calendar Case.

entities.text: Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Addanki, Prakasam district
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Reliance has been placed on an unreported judgment, dated 18.12.2019, passed in Criminal Petition No.5421 of 2019 and other connected cases and also a common order passed by a learned single Judge of this Court, dated 27.08.2018, in Criminal Petition No.3731 of 2018 and other connected cases.

4. By way of placing the charge sheet, learned counsel for the petitioners has argued that save except recovery of tobacco products, which are prohibited under the FSS Act, no other cognizable offence is made out.

In present matter, it appears that the Police with a view to usurp jurisdiction of lodging FIR, in a case of recovery of tobacco, which is prohibited under the FSS Act, has mechanically incorporated Sections 273 and 188 R/w.34 of IPC.

He submits that since in an identical situation,
this Court has RK,J interfered with the FIR and also during initial investigation, this Court may pass similar order.
5.

Learned Public Prosecutor has tried to persuade the Court that if a cognizable offence under the provisions of IPC is made out along with the offences under the FSS Act, the Police is having jurisdiction to lodge the FIR and investigate the same.
However, he has not distinguished the present case with the cases on which reliance was placed by learned counsel for the petitioners.

6. Besides hearing learned counsel for the parties and after going through the charge sheet, it is evident that save except recovery of tobacco products and also confession of the petitioners before the Police, there is no fact disclosing the commission of offence under the IPC and as such following judgment of this Court, referred supra, I have no option except to interfere with the same.
7.
Accordingly, the proceedings in C.C. No.659 of 2018 on the file of learned Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Addanki, Prakasam district, are hereby quashed.

entities.text: Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Addanki, Prakasam district
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Consequently, the Criminal Petition stands allowed.

8. As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, in this case shall stand closed.
